findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete automated assertion to AC4 — e.g. pipe `rebar explain T15` through a `python -c` or `grep -q` that asserts all required strings are present, matching the pattern of ACs 1–3 and 5–6.
evidence: AC4 reads: 'rebar explain T15 prints the criterion name, exec tier AGENT, facet overlay-derisk, and the rubric body (S1-S3 + checks a-d)' — no grep/assert follows
All other ACs use `python -c '…; assert …'` patterns that fail-fast on wrong values
No `| grep -q` or pipe-to-assert wraps the rebar explain call
findings.finding: AC4 ('rebar explain T15 prints …') has no automated assertion command — an agent must visually inspect the output rather than running a deterministic assert that produces evidence on success, making the proving command weaker than the other five ACs.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC4: `rebar explain T15` bullet
scenarios: An agent runs `rebar explain T15`, sees output, marks AC complete, but the output actually omits 'S3' or 'PROVE-THEN-CODIFY' due to a rendering bug — no assertion catches it
CI cannot automate AC4 without an assertion; visual inspection is error-prone
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the prose description with: `python -c "import subprocess, sys; out=subprocess.check_output(['rebar','explain','T15'],text=True); missing=[k for k in ['overlay-derisk','AGENT','S1','S3','RISK NAMED','PROVE-THEN-CODIFY','SCOPED CLEANUP','ANTI-FP'] if k not in out]; sys.exit(bool(missing)) or print('OK')"` exits 0.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a programmatic verify command to AC 4, e.g. `python -c "import subprocess; out=subprocess.check_output(['rebar','explain','T15'],text=True); assert all(k in out for k in ['overlay-derisk','AGENT','S1','S2','S3','RISK NAMED','PROVE-THEN-CODIFY'])"` (or equivalent), consistent with the other ACs.

findings.finding: AC 4 (`rebar explain T15`) has no programmatic verify command, unlike every other AC (1-3, 5-6 all have explicit `python -c ...` scripts). The AC text says 'prints the criterion name, exec tier AGENT, facet overlay-derisk, and the rubric body' but provides no machine-executable check, making it the only unverifiable AC in the set.
scenarios: An implementer ships a broken `rebar explain` invocation and no automated check catches it during CI validation of the ACs.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to AC 4: `Verify: python -c "import subprocess; out=subprocess.check_output(['rebar','explain','T15'],text=True); assert all(k in out for k in ['overlay-derisk','AGENT','S1','RISK NAMED','PROVE-THEN-CODIFY','SCOPED CLEANUP','ANTI-FP']), out"`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `'T15'` to the `AGENT_TIER` frozenset in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` (Step 3), or explicitly document why T15 intentionally relies on the `exec_tier()` OR-fallback instead of AGENT_TIER membership (as every other AGENT-exec overlay is in AGENT_TIER).
evidence: Step 3 says only: 'Add "T15" to CANONICAL_LLM in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py'
AGENT_TIER frozenset contains T1, T3, T5c, T8, T10, T11 — all AGENT-exec overlays — but the plan makes no mention of it

exec_tier() at line 517: `crit.get('id') in AGENT_TIER or str(crit.get('exec','')).upper() == 'AGENT'` — OR branch means runtime behavior is correct, but the omission from AGENT_TIER is an unenumerated edit
findings.finding: The plan's Step 3 adds T15 only to `CANONICAL_LLM` in registry.py, but omits adding T15 to the `AGENT_TIER` frozenset in the same file. Every other AGENT-exec overlay (T1, T3, T5c, T8, T10, T11) is listed in `AGENT_TIER`. While `exec_tier()` has an OR-fallback (`str(crit.get('exec','')).upper() == 'AGENT'`) that catches T15 via its routing entry's `exec: 'AGENT'` field, the plan neither adds T15 to `AGENT_TIER` nor acknowledges the intentional omission — leaving the established pattern unacknowledged and `AGENT_TIER`'s documented purpose as the authoritative agent-tier set inconsistent.
scenarios: A developer reading AGENT_TIER as the authoritative list of agent-tier criteria would conclude T15 is NOT agent-tier, since it is absent from the frozenset while all peer criteria are present.
If a future refactor removes the exec-field OR-branch from exec_tier() (relying solely on AGENT_TIER membership), T15 would silently downgrade to 1-TURN dispatch.
findings.suggested_fix: In Step 3, extend the instruction to: 'Add "T15" to CANONICAL_LLM and to AGENT_TIER in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py.' Add a corresponding AC assertion: `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.registry import AGENT_TIER; assert 'T15' in AGENT_TIER"`.

findings.finding: The plan prescribes `execution_mode: AGENT` verbatim in the T15 front-matter (both in the rubric-to-write section and in AC line 1), but the prompt loader's EXECUTION_MODES closed enum is `("single_turn", "agentic")` — `"AGENT"` is not a valid value and will cause the prompt loader to raise an error at load time. Every existing AGENT-tier plan-review rubric (T13, T14, T1, T3, T5c, T8, T10, T11, G1G2, etc.) uses `execution_mode: agentic`.
findings.location: Rubric to write section (front-matter) + AC line 1: `execution_mode: AGENT`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace every occurrence of `execution_mode: AGENT` in the plan (rubric front-matter spec + AC line 1) with `execution_mode: agentic` — matching the closed enum in `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:74` and the established pattern in all existing AGENT-tier rubrics (T13, T14, T1, etc.).

findings.finding: The plan specifies `execution_mode: AGENT` in the T15 front-matter, but the valid enum values recognized by the prompt loader are `'single_turn'` and `'agentic'` — `'AGENT'` (uppercase) is not in `EXECUTION_MODES` and will raise a `ReviewerError` at load time, failing `check_registry_coverage`.
findings.location: ## Rubric to write verbatim into src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T15.md — YAML front-matter line `execution_mode: AGENT`; also AC line 1
findings.suggested_fix: In the plan's verbatim front-matter spec, replace `execution_mode: AGENT` with `execution_mode: agentic` (matching all existing AGENT-tier criterion files such as plan_review_T13.md and plan_review_T14.md).

findings.finding: The plan instructs writing `execution_mode: AGENT` in the plan_review_T15.md front-matter, but the prompt-loading machinery only accepts `agentic` (and `single_turn`) as valid execution_mode values. Every existing AGENT-tier rubric file in the codebase uses `execution_mode: agentic`. Writing `AGENT` will cause `get_prompt` to raise a validation error, making `check_registry_coverage`, `rebar explain T15`, and the guide regeneration all fail — breaking at least four of the six ACs.
findings.location: Rubric to write verbatim into src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T15.md — YAML front-matter spec
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `execution_mode: AGENT` with `execution_mode: agentic` in the YAML front-matter block. The routing entry in criteria_routing.json correctly keeps `"exec": "AGENT"` — that value feeds the registry's exec_tier() dispatch and is a separate concern from the prompt-level execution_mode.

findings.finding: The plan specifies `execution_mode: AGENT` in the plan_review_T15.md front-matter, but the prompt loader's closed enum EXECUTION_MODES = ('single_turn', 'agentic') does not include 'AGENT'. The loader raises PromptError for any unlisted value, causing check_registry_coverage to report T15 as unloadable and the registry validators (AC5) to fail.
findings.location: ## Rubric to write verbatim into src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T15.md — YAML front-matter field `execution_mode: AGENT`
findings.suggested_fix: In the YAML front-matter block, replace `execution_mode: AGENT` with `execution_mode: agentic`. This matches every other AGENT-tier criterion file in the prompt library (T8, T13, T14, G1G2, etc.) and satisfies the EXECUTION_MODES closed enum.

findings.finding: AC line 5 names `validate_routing` as one of the registry-validator functions to check, but the actual importable function in `registry.py` is `validate_packaged_routing` — there is no `validate_routing` symbol exported from that module.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `validate_routing` with `validate_packaged_routing` in AC bullet 5, or note that the CLI equivalent is `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry validate-routing`.

findings.finding: AC2's proving command (`grep '"T15"' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`) only confirms the key string is present; it does NOT verify the required field values (exec: AGENT, facet: overlay-derisk, overlay_routing: llm, applies_at.suppress_types: ["bug"]) that the AC text claims to prove. A grep on the key alone passes even if all field values are wrong.
findings.suggested_fix:
```
jq -e '.T15 | select(.exec=="AGENT" and .facet=="overlay-derisk" and .overlay_routing=="llm" and (.applies_at.suppress_types | index("bug") != null))' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json
```

findings.finding: AC6's proving command (`grep -A2 '^## T15' docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`) prints only the 2 lines immediately after the heading, which is insufficient to verify the AC's claim that the generated section 'matches the rubric' — the T15 rubric body spans many lines (S1–S3 gate, checks a–d, ANTI-FP paragraph).
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC6 with: `grep -A2 '^## T15' docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md && grep -c 'PROVE-THEN-CODIFY\|SCOPED CLEANUP\|overlay-derisk' docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md | grep -q '[3-9]'`
